Class IdentityDbContextBase<TUser, TRole, TIdentityKey>

Namespace
NuvTools.Security.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore
Assembly
NuvTools.Security.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore.dll

Provides a base implementation of IdentityDbContext<TUser, TRole, TKey> with enhanced transaction support, execution strategies, and batch operation capabilities.

public abstract class IdentityDbContextBase<TUser, TRole, TIdentityKey> : IdentityDbContext<TUser, TRole, TIdentityKey>, IInfrastructure<IServiceProvider>, IDbContextDependencies, IDbSetCache, IDbContextPoolable, IResettableService, IDisposable, IAsyncDisposable, IDbContextCommands, IDbContextWithListCommands where TUser : IdentityUser<TIdentityKey> where TRole : IdentityRole<TIdentityKey> where TIdentityKey : IEquatable<TIdentityKey>

Type Parameters

TUser

The type representing a user in the system, must inherit from IdentityUser<TKey>.

TRole

The type representing a role in the system, must inherit from IdentityRole<TKey>.

TIdentityKey

The type of the primary key for users and roles, must implement IEquatable<T>.

Examples

public class ApplicationDbContext : IdentityDbContextBase<ApplicationUser, ApplicationRole, Guid>
{
    public ApplicationDbContext(DbContextOptions<ApplicationDbContext> options)
        : base(options)
    {
    }

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder builder)
    {
        base.OnModelCreating(builder);
        // Configure your entities here
    }
}

Remarks

This abstract base class extends IdentityDbContext<TUser, TRole, TKey> and implements IDbContextCommands and IDbContextWithListCommands to provide:

  • Transaction management with begin, commit, and rollback operations
  • Execution strategies for handling transient database failures
  • Convenient CRUD operations that automatically save changes and return IResult wrappers
  • Batch operations for synchronizing collections of entities
  • Support for composite key operations

All operations use the Result pattern, returning IResult or IResult<T> instead of throwing exceptions for business logic failures.

AddOrRemoveFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity>, Func<TEntity, TKey>, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>?, CancellationToken)

Asynchronously adds new entities from a collection or removes existing ones that are not in the collection, without updating existing entities.

public Task<IResult> AddOrRemoveFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity> entities, Func<TEntity, TKey> keySelector, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>? filter = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) where TEntity : class where TKey : notnull

Parameters

entities IEnumerable<TEntity>

The collection of entities to ensure exist in the database.

keySelector Func<TEntity, TKey>

A function to extract the key from an entity for comparison.

filter Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>

An optional filter expression to limit which database entities are considered for removal.

cancellationToken CancellationToken

A CancellationToken to observe while waiting for the task to complete.

Returns

Task<IResult>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains an IResult indicating whether the operation was successful.

Type Parameters

TEntity

The type of entity to add or remove. Must be a reference type.

TKey

The type of the key used to identify entities. Must be non-nullable.

Examples

// Ensure specific tags exist for a post without updating existing tag data
var tags = new[] { "C#", "ASP.NET", "EF Core" }.Select(t => new Tag { Name = t, PostId = postId });
await context.AddOrRemoveFromListAsync(tags, t => t.Name, t => t.PostId == postId);

Remarks

This method performs selective add/remove operations:

  • Entities in the collection but not in the database are added
  • Entities in the database (matching the filter) but not in the collection are removed
  • Existing entities that are in both the collection and database are left unchanged (not updated)

This is useful when you only care about the presence of entities, not their current values.

AddOrUpdateFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity>, Func<TEntity, TKey>, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>?, CancellationToken)

Asynchronously adds new entities from a collection or updates existing ones, without removing any entities.

public Task<IResult> AddOrUpdateFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity> entities, Func<TEntity, TKey> keySelector, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>? filter = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) where TEntity : class where TKey : notnull

Parameters

entities IEnumerable<TEntity>

The collection of entities to add or update in the database.

keySelector Func<TEntity, TKey>

A function to extract the key from an entity for comparison.

filter Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>

An optional filter expression to limit which database entities are considered for matching.

cancellationToken CancellationToken

A CancellationToken to observe while waiting for the task to complete.

Returns

Task<IResult>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains an IResult indicating whether the operation was successful.

Type Parameters

TEntity

The type of entity to add or update. Must be a reference type.

TKey

The type of the key used to identify entities. Must be non-nullable.

Examples

// Add or update permissions without removing existing ones
var permissions = new[] { "Read", "Write", "Execute" }.Select(p => new Permission { Name = p });
await context.AddOrUpdateFromListAsync(permissions, p => p.Name);

Remarks

This method performs an upsert operation:

  • Entities not found in the database are added
  • Entities found in the database are updated with values from the collection
  • No entities are removed from the database

This is useful when you want to ensure certain entities exist and are up-to-date without deleting others.

BeginTransactionAsync(CancellationToken)

Asynchronously begins a new database transaction.

public Task<IDbContextTransaction> BeginTransactionAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Parameters

cancellationToken CancellationToken

A CancellationToken to observe while waiting for the task to complete.

Returns

Task<IDbContextTransaction>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains an IDbContextTransaction that represents the started transaction.

Remarks

Transactions allow multiple database operations to be executed as a single atomic unit. Use CommitTransactionAsync(CancellationToken) to commit the transaction or RollbackTransactionAsync(CancellationToken) to roll it back.

CommitTransactionAsync(CancellationToken)

Parameters

cancellationToken CancellationToken

Returns

Task

A task that represents the asynchronous operation.

Remarks

This method should be called after BeginTransactionAsync(CancellationToken) to persist the changes. If the commit fails, the transaction remains active and can be rolled back.

SyncFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity>, Func<TEntity, TKey>, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>?, CancellationToken)

Asynchronously synchronizes a collection of entities with the database by adding new entities, updating existing ones, and removing entities not present in the collection.

public Task<IResult> SyncFromListAsync<TEntity, TKey>(IEnumerable<TEntity> entities, Func<TEntity, TKey> keySelector, Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>? filter = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) where TEntity : class where TKey : notnull

Parameters

entities IEnumerable<TEntity>

The collection of entities to synchronize with the database.

keySelector Func<TEntity, TKey>

A function to extract the key from an entity for comparison.

filter Expression<Func<TEntity, bool>>

An optional filter expression to limit which database entities are considered for synchronization.

cancellationToken CancellationToken

A CancellationToken to observe while waiting for the task to complete.

Returns

Task<IResult>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains an IResult indicating whether the synchronization was successful.

Type Parameters

TEntity

The type of entity to synchronize. Must be a reference type.

TKey

The type of the key used to identify entities. Must be non-nullable.

Examples

// Synchronize user roles - adds new, updates existing, removes missing
var userRoles = newRoleIds.Select(roleId => new IdentityUserRole<Guid> { UserId = userId, RoleId = roleId });
await context.SyncFromListAsync(userRoles, ur => ur.RoleId, ur => ur.UserId == userId);

Remarks

This method performs a full synchronization:

  • Entities in the collection but not in the database are added
  • Entities in both the collection and database are updated with values from the collection
  • Entities in the database (matching the filter) but not in the collection are removed

This is useful for maintaining master-detail relationships or synchronizing complete lists.
